scores.label: A
scores.note: Option 10 'remarkable' is 0: it changes the sense from size to surprising or extraordinary, and it reads as praise for what is mostly a harmful effect. 'notable' and 'noteworthy' are about being worth noticing, not size. 'important' needs 'an' instead of 'a'. The six strong options come first.

scores.label: B
scores.note: No judged option is 0. Options 5-10 are duplicates (code fail), so the list has only four distinct words. 'large' is plain. 'important' needs 'an' and changes the sense to importance.

scores.label: C
scores.note: No judged option is 0. Options 5 and 9 repeat 'considerable' (code fail). 'meaningful', 'noteworthy' and 'notable' drift from size toward significance or being worth noticing. The strong options come first.

scores.label: D
scores.note: Option 8 'extensive' is 0: 'an extensive effect' is an awkward pairing (extensive means wide in scope), and it also needs 'an' instead of 'a'. 'serious' adds a negative judgment the opening sentence doesn't make. 'dramatic' is a bit stronger than 'big'. 'great' can be misread as 'excellent'. The strong options come first.

scores.label: E
scores.note: No judged option is 0. Option 8 repeats 'considerable' (code fail). 'profound' raises the strength slightly but is a standard essay word. 'deep' is a less common pairing with 'effect'. 'great' can be misread as 'excellent'. 'notable' is about being worth noticing, not size.
